references.text: When the Samaritans settled in the land, they did not know how to worship the Lord. They mixed idolatry with the worship of Israel's God – they worshipped what they did not know ([ref:2 Kings 17:29-41|2 Kings 17:29-41]).
God made known His words and His laws to Israel, something He did not do for any other nation. Salvation and true revelation came through the Jews ([ref:Psalms 147:19-20|Psalms 147:19-20]).
The prophecy that the Lord's law shall go out from Zion and the Lord's word from Jerusalem confirms that salvation is from the Jews ([ref:Isaiah 2:3|Isaiah 2:3]).
God's promise to Abraham that in him all families of the earth would be blessed shows that salvation comes through the Jews ([ref:Genesis 12:3|Genesis 12:3]).
Jacob's prophecy that the scepter shall not depart from Judah points to the fact that the Messiah and salvation are to come from the Jews ([ref:Genesis 49:10|Genesis 49:10]).
Paul emphasizes that the Jews were entrusted with God's words, which confirms Jesus' statement that salvation is from the Jews ([ref:Romans 3:1-2|Romans 3:1-2]).
The people of Israel received adoption, glory, covenants, the law, worship, and promises – and from them comes Christ according to the flesh ([ref:Romans 9:4-5|Romans 9:4-5]).
The Lord's servant, who comes from Israel, shall be a light for the nations and bring salvation to the ends of the earth ([ref:Isaiah 49:6|Isaiah 49:6]).
In Jesus' name, repentance and forgiveness of sins are to be proclaimed to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem – salvation goes out from the Jews ([ref:Luke 24:47|Luke 24:47]).
Jesus continues by explaining that true worship takes place in spirit and truth – an elaboration on the contrast between ignorance and true worship ([ref:John 4:23-24|John 4:23-24]).
In Judah God is known, in Israel His name is great – true knowledge of God was with the Jews ([ref:Psalms 76:2|Psalms 76:2]).
